sentences.text: THIS WRIT APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 4 OF THE KARNATAKA HIGH COURT ACT PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE ORDER PASSED BY THE HON'BLE LEARNED SINGLE JUDGE IN THE WRIT PETITION Nos.18071-18072/2014 DATED 15/03/2016.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JAYANT BANERJI  and  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. V. ARAVIND
ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JAYANT BANERJI)

The aforesaid appeal has been filed seeking to set aside the order dated 15.03.2016 passed by the learned Single Judge in Writ Petition Nos.18071-18072/2014 whereby, while referring to the provision of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
20131

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
20131
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: it was held
that possession
had not been taken in Act of 2013 NC: 2025:KHC:50462-DB HC-KAR respect of 16 guntas of land in Survey No.146/A of Agara Village therefore, not only the scheme would lapse but the acquisition as well.
Accordingly, the petition was allowed.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant has referred to the judgment of this Court in the case of L.
Ramareddy v. State of Karnataka, Urban Development Department, represented by Secretary and Others2 to contend that in respect of the same notifications pertaining to the same Survey No.146 of Agara Village, a Division Bench of this Court has observed that the provision of sub-section (2) of Section 24 of the Act of 2013 would not apply to acquisitions initiated under the provisions of any other enactment particularly, State enactments such as the Bangalore Development Act, 19763.

2 Others4.
3.

entities.text: HC-KAR Development Authority and Another v. State of Karnataka and Bangalore Development Authority vs Sri. S. Venkata Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have perused the record of the other Writ Appeal bearing No.1415/2018, which is the case of L. Ramareddy referred above as well as the original record produced by learned counsel for the Bangalore Development Authority5 and we find that the preliminary and final notifications issued under the BDA Act, which were subjected to challenge in L. Ramareddy, are also in respect of the aforesaid Survey No.146 of Agara Village, which was under challenge in W.P. Nos.18071- 18072/2014.

4. In view of the aforesaid, the order of the learned Single Judge of 15.03.2016, which is impugned in this writ appeal, in Writ Petition Nos.18071-18072/2014 cannot stand and is accordingly, set aside.
